ideas.pitch: An AI-powered debugging and code refactoring platform specifically targeted at C, Java, and Python syntax traps often found in competitive programming and academic exams.
ideas.title: SyntaxSage
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly aligns with the Department of Computer Applications' focus on debugging skills and logic testing, appealing to faculty judges who want to see tooling for academic and competitive programming.

ideas.pitch: A visual algorithm dependency mapper that takes dense competitive programming problems and generates graph intelligence showing optimal data structures and time complexity pathways.
ideas.title: LogicGraph
ideas.why_it_could_win: Showcases genuinely hard engineering by parsing code logic into graph representations, reflecting patterns from top-tier technical hackathon winners.

ideas.pitch: A real-time collaborative pair-programming environment designed exclusively for teams of two, featuring synchronized AST analysis to prevent conflicting logic blocks during timed hackathon sprints.
ideas.title: CodeDuet
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targeted precisely at the strict two-member team constraint of Optiquest, solving the exact bottleneck duos face when working under tight time limits.

ideas.pitch: An automated complexity analyzer that profiles Python, Java, and C solutions against edge-case test suites, predicting memory limits and TLEs before submission.
ideas.title: ByteMetric
ideas.why_it_could_win: Appeals directly to the programming competition and problem-solving abilities emphasized by the R.V.R. & J.C. College of Engineering event organizers.

ideas.pitch: An automated question bank generator that uses AST parsing on GitHub repositories to instantly create multi-level C, Java, and Python multiple-choice questions for technical tests.
ideas.title: MCQGen
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors the prelim format of Optiquest (MCQs covering C, Java, and Python syntax), offering immediate practical utility for the event's organizers and department.
